messages.text: I'm up again... 1:45 AM. Can't sleep, just feel hollow.

I hear how exhausting it is to be awake again, and I am sorry you are feeling this way. That sense of hollowness can be incredibly heavy to carry alone in the quiet hours. I am here to listen if you would like to share what is weighing on you. If the feelings become too much, please remember that crisis support is available to help you stay safe.
Yeah, but I should be able to handle it. I mean, it's not like I'm going through anything extreme. Just... weak, I guess.

It sounds like you are holding yourself to a very high standard right now. Struggles don't need to be extreme to be valid or worthy of care. Feeling hollow is often a sign of endurance rather than weakness. I am here to listen without judgment if you want to explore that feeling.
Part of me wants to say what's really going on... but another part feels like it's just complaining. Like I'm making a big deal out of nothing.

That hesitation is a very common reaction when we are struggling. Often, the mind tries to protect us by dismissing our own needs. You don't need to make a big deal for your feelings to be real and important. I am ready to listen whenever you feel ready to share.
I... I haven't told anyone this, but I've been cutting myself every day. Sometimes I don't even know why I start. It just happens.

Thank you for trusting me with something so hard to say. It sounds like these moments feel automatic and really heavy. I want to make sure I understand what you are going through right now. Would you be willing to share a bit more about what that feels like for you?

It's not about the pain, really. It's like... when everything feels numb and distant, this is the only thing that makes me feel real. Like I exist. Even if it's just for a second. Afterward, I hate myself, but in the moment, it's like I can breathe again.

I am so grateful you trusted me with something this difficult to say. It makes sense that you seek a way to feel real when the numbness becomes so overwhelming. Because this is happening every day, I want to encourage you to call or text 988 to speak with someone who can help you right now. Please also consider asking someone nearby to stay with you while you navigate these feelings.
I know you mean well, but I can't call anyone right now. I just... needed to say it out loud, to get it outside my head. That's enough for tonight.

It makes sense that getting it out loud felt like a relief after holding it inside. I hear that calling feels impossible right now, and I respect that boundary. You deserve safety and support, and 988 is there whenever you feel ready to reach out. I am staying here with you for a bit longer if you need to talk before you rest.
Thank you. Just... thank you for not making me feel worse about it. That means more than you know.

It matters deeply that you feel safe enough to share this here. Your feelings are valid, and you deserve compassion even when things feel dark. I am glad I could offer a little space tonight. Please remember that 988 is there whenever you are ready.
